'''Askold Georgievich Khovanskii''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} ({{langx|ru|Аскольд Георгиевич Хованский}}; born 3 June 1947) is a [[Russian people|Russian]]-[[Canadians|Canadian]] [[mathematician]] currently at the [[University of Toronto]].<ref>[https://www.math.toronto.edu/askold/newcvWWW.pdf Askold Khovanskii's CV]</ref> His areas of research are [[algebraic geometry]], [[commutative algebra]], [[singularity theory]], [[differential geometry]] and [[differential equation]]s. His research is in the development of the theory of [[toric variety|toric varieties]] and [[Newton polytope|Newton polyhedra]] in algebraic geometry. He is also the inventor of the theory of [[Sparse polynomial|fewnomials]], and the [[Bernstein–Khovanskii–Kushnirenko theorem]] is named after him.

He obtained his Ph.D. in 1973 from the [[Steklov Mathematical Institute]] in Moscow under the supervision of [[Vladimir Arnold]].<ref>https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=49054</ref> In his [[Ph.D.]] thesis, he developed a [[Topological Galois theory|topological version]] of [[Galois theory]]. He studied the theory of [[Newton-Okounkov body|Newton–Okounkov bodies]].

Among his graduate students are Olga Gel'fond, Feodor Borodich, H. Petrov-Tan'kin, Kiumars Kaveh,<ref>[https://www.pitt.edu/~kaveh/ Home page of Kiumars Kaveh]</ref> Farzali Izadi, Ivan Soprunov,<ref>[https://academic.csuohio.edu/soprunov-ivan/ Home page of Ivan Soprunov]</ref> Jenya Soprunova,<ref>[https://www.math.kent.edu/~soprunova/ Home page of Jenya Soprunova]</ref>  Vladlen Timorin,<ref>[https://www.hse.ru/en/org/persons/10023259 Home page of Vladlen Timorin]</ref> Valentina Kirichenko,<ref>[https://www.hse.ru/en/org/persons/22565285 Home page of Valentina Kiritchenko]</ref> Sergey Chulkov, V. Kisunko, Mikhail Mazin,<ref>[https://www.math.ksu.edu/~mmazin/ Home page of Mikhail Mazin]</ref> O. Ivrii, K. Matveev, Yuri Burda, and J. Yang.

In 2014, he received the [[Jeffery–Williams Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] for outstanding contributions to mathematical research in Canada.<ref>[http://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2014/jw-prize.html Canadian Mathematical Society: University of Toronto professor garners prestigious national award], retrieved 2015-04-07.</ref> He was elected to the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 2020.<ref>https://rsc-src.ca/en/users/askold-khovanskii</ref>
